extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, school administrators, legal practitioners, and public commenters interested in Title IX athletics rulemaking
extracted.subtask_short: search results for Title IX athletics
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register search-results listing of documents (proposed rules, final rules, notices, and related materials) addressing Title IX as applied to athletics. The page aggregates excerpts that state regulatory standards, exceptions, definitions, and procedural obligations relevant to athletic-team eligibility and Title IX compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Title IX athletics standard governing sex-related eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed regulatory standard that would govern a recipient's adoption or application of sex-related criteria that would limit or deny a student's eligibility to participate on a male or female athletic team consistent with their gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section describing the Athletics NPRM: the regulation would clarify Title IX's application to sex-related criteria and the obligation of schools/recipients that adopt or apply such criteria to do so consistent with Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must provide educational environment free from sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of Federal financial assistance must provide an educational environment free from discrimination on the basis of sex, including through responding to incidents of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to elementary, secondary, postsecondary institutions and other recipients; amendments are intended to align regulatory requirements with Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate and to clarify scope and recipient obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process requirements for sexual harassment under Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must resolve allegations of sexual harassment promptly and accurately under a predictable, fair grievance process that provides due process protections to alleged victims and alleged perpetrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations obligate recipients to respond promptly and supportively to persons alleged to be victimized, to implement effective remedies, and to prohibit retaliation; also clarify interaction with Constitutional protections and other laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and supportive response to alleged sexual harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to respond promptly and supportively to persons alleged to be victimized by sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of Title IX obligations to address sexual harassment as a form of sex discrimination; ties into grievance process, remedies, and coordinator responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and dissemination of Title IX Coordinator and non-discrimination policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recipient must designate a Title IX Coordinator and disseminate the recipient's non-discrimination policy and contact information for the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required by the final regulations as part of institutional obligations to address sex discrimination and ensure members of the community can access Title IX processes and supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and retention of Title IX statutory exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory text should (or must) reflect Title IX's statutory exceptions as set forth in 20 U.S.C. 1681(a)(1)-(9); the Department declined to remove reference to those exceptions from §106.1 because they are an important component of the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges that regulatory language should be consistent with statutory exceptions and that omission could mislead readers about available exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous requirement to allow opposite-sex tryouts for single-sex teams (and subsequent amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing regulations had required certain recipients sponsoring sports teams for members of one sex to allow members of the opposite sex to try out for the team; a DFR amends those regulations so these requirements will no longer be a factor when recipients operate sports teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prior rule: 'members of the excluded sex must be allowed to try out for the team offered unless the sport involved is a contact sport.' The DFR removes/changes the effect of that requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact sport exception / definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the 'allow to try out' requirement, contact sports include boxing, wrestling, rugby, ice hockey, football, basketball, and other sports the purpose or major activity of which involves bodily contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the exception to the opposite-sex tryout requirement in prior regulations; included verbatim enumerated examples in excerpts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable provisions considering the nature of particular sports
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory implementations of Title IX (per Education Amendments of 1974 section 844) should include 'reasonable provisions considering the nature of particular sports.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that athletic-specific considerations (e.g., physiological differences, safety, nature of sport) may be relevant when applying Title IX in athletics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide discretion and flexibility to account for school variations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed regulations would enable all schools to meet Title IX obligations while providing appropriate discretion and flexibility to account for variations in school size, student populations, and administrative structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges practical differences among institutions and intends to allow recipients to implement Title IX obligations consistent with local circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscriminatory distribution of federal funds (including emergency grants) under civil-rights laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not distribute emergency financial aid grants or other federally funded assistance in a manner that discriminates against individuals on the basis of race, color, national origin, disability, or sex (including under Title IX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited in a HEERF notice as an example of Title IX and other civil-rights obligations that accompany receipt of federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of Title IX regulations with nondiscrimination mandate and intersection with other laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory amendments aim to better align Title IX regulatory requirements with Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate and clarify how Title IX interacts with Constitutional protections, Title VII, FERPA, and other laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides drafting and interpretation of regulations so that Title IX enforcement is consistent with other legal obligations and rights.
